lit: to turn one's back on the village well and leave one's native place

use.how: Predicate or attributive (背井离乡的打工者). Said with sympathy of people who leave home for a long time out of hardship: work, war, famine.

near.diff: 流离失所 stresses being homeless and drifting with nowhere to live; 背井离乡 stresses having left one's home region far behind.

cue: Floods ruined the farms, and whole families had to leave their native village to look for work in distant cities. What did they have to do?

ctx.s: 为了给家里挣钱，他十八岁就{背井离乡}，到南方打工。
ctx.en: To earn money for his family, he left home at eighteen to work in the south.

ctx.s: 战争让成千上万的人{背井离乡}，失去了家园。
ctx.en: The war drove tens of thousands of people from their homeland and left them without homes.

ctx.s: 奶奶常说：“当年{背井离乡}的滋味，我这辈子都忘不了。”
ctx.en: Grandma often says: "I'll never forget what it felt like to leave home back then."

ctx.s: 这部电影讲的是一群{背井离乡}的年轻人在大城市奋斗的故事。
ctx.en: The film tells the story of a group of young people far from home, struggling to make it in a big city.

ctx.s: 你一个人在外地工作，{背井离乡}的，过年总该回家看看吧？
ctx.en: You're working alone so far from home; surely you'll come back for the New Year?

ctx.s: 那年大旱，村里许多人家不得不{背井离乡}，外出谋生。
ctx.en: That year of the great drought, many families in the village had to leave home to make a living elsewhere.

bad.s: 暑假我们全家{背井离乡}，去海边玩了一个星期。
bad.en: (meant: in the summer holidays our family went to the seaside for a week)
bad.why: It describes leaving one's home region for a long time out of hardship, not a holiday trip.

bad.s: 他从城东搬到城西，算是{背井离乡}了。
bad.en: (meant: he moved from the east of the city to the west)
bad.why: Moving across town is not leaving one's native place; the idiom implies going far away, usually under pressure.

lit: a bright pearl held in the palm of the hand

story.text: The image goes back to the poem 'Short Song' by Fu Xuan of the Western Jin dynasty, in which a woman abandoned by the man she loved laments that he once looked on her like a pearl in his palm and has now thrown her away into a ditch. Later the pearl in the palm came to mean a much-loved child, above all a daughter.

use.how: A noun, object of 是, 当作 or 视为: 她是父母的掌上明珠。 Said affectionately of a daughter cherished by her parents.

near.diff: 心肝宝贝 is colloquial and used for any dearly loved person or child; 掌上明珠 is more literary and almost always a daughter.

cue: An only daughter whose parents adore her, keep her photo on every desk and would do anything for her. What is she to them?

ctx.s: 小雨是家里的独生女，从小就是父母的{掌上明珠}。
ctx.en: Xiaoyu is an only daughter and has been her parents' darling since she was little.

ctx.s: 老王把女儿视为{掌上明珠}，什么事都依着她。
ctx.en: Old Wang treasures his daughter and gives in to her on everything.

ctx.s: “你可是我们的{掌上明珠}，出国留学一定要照顾好自己。”妈妈叮嘱道。
ctx.en: "You're our precious girl; take good care of yourself while you study abroad," her mother urged.

ctx.s: 婚礼上，新娘的父亲红着眼眶说：“今天我把{掌上明珠}交给你了。”
ctx.en: At the wedding the bride's father said, eyes red: "Today I'm handing you my precious daughter."

ctx.s: 她虽是富商的{掌上明珠}，却一点也不娇气。
ctx.en: Although she is a rich businessman's beloved daughter, she isn't spoiled at all.

ctx.s: 谁不知道这个小姑娘是全家的{掌上明珠}？
ctx.en: Who doesn't know that this little girl is the darling of the whole family?

bad.s: 我的{掌上明珠}摔坏了，得拿去修。
bad.en: (meant: my treasured phone got broken and needs repairing)
bad.why: It is said of a cherished daughter, not of a prized possession.

bad.s: 父母很{掌上明珠}她。
bad.en: (meant: her parents cherish her very much)
bad.why: It is a noun, not a verb: a daughter can be her parents' pearl, but parents cannot 'pearl' her.

lit: born delicate and brought up indulged

use.how: Predicate or attributive (娇生惯养的孩子). Said of how a person was raised, criticising the softness or helplessness that results.

near.diff: 养尊处优 is an adult living in comfort thanks to status or wealth; 娇生惯养 is about being spoiled while growing up.

cue: A twenty-year-old has never cooked, washed his own clothes or carried his own bags, because his parents always did everything for him. How was he raised?

ctx.s: 他从小{娇生惯养}，连袜子都没自己洗过。
ctx.en: He was pampered from childhood and has never even washed his own socks.

ctx.s: 别看她是{娇生惯养}长大的，干起活来一点也不怕苦。
ctx.en: She may have been raised pampered, but when she works she doesn't shy away from hardship at all.

ctx.s: 老师对家长说：“孩子不能太{娇生惯养}，该做的家务要让他自己做。”
ctx.en: The teacher told the parents: "Don't spoil the child too much; let him do the chores he should do."

ctx.s: 不少{娇生惯养}的城市孩子，第一次参加夏令营就哭着要回家。
ctx.en: Quite a few pampered city kids cry to go home at their first summer camp.

ctx.s: 你都三十岁了，还这么{娇生惯养}，以后怎么独立生活？
ctx.en: You're thirty and still so spoiled; how will you ever live on your own?

ctx.s: 小说里的大少爷{娇生惯养}，家道中落后吃尽了苦头。
ctx.en: The young master in the novel was raised in luxury, and suffered terribly once the family fortune collapsed.

bad.s: 我奶奶对花草{娇生惯养}，每天浇水三次。
bad.en: (meant: my grandma lovingly cares for her plants)
bad.why: It describes a person who was spoiled growing up, not someone caring for something.

bad.s: 这位老师{娇生惯养}学生，大家都很喜欢他。
bad.en: (meant: this teacher is very kind to his students)
bad.why: It takes no object and is criticism of the spoiled person, not praise of a kind giver.

mean: a platitude, the same old advice
lit: the everyday talk of an old scholar

story.text: In the Three Kingdoms period the powerful minister He Yan asked the diviner Guan Lu to read his fortune. Guan Lu warned him to be humble and cautious if he wished to escape disaster. Deng Yang, who was with them, scoffed that this was only the everyday talk of an old scholar. Not long afterwards both He Yan and Deng Yang were put to death.

use.how: A noun, often after 是 or in 虽然是老生常谈，但…. Said of advice or views everyone has heard many times; often used modestly about one's own reminder.

near.diff: 陈词滥调 is stale, empty phrasing and is harsher; 老生常谈 is familiar, often-repeated advice that may still be true.

cue: Before every exam your father repeats the same advice: sleep early, read each question twice. You have heard it a hundred times. What is his advice?

ctx.s: 妈妈又开始讲“早睡早起身体好”，这都是{老生常谈}了。
ctx.en: Mum is on about "early to bed, early to rise" again; we've heard it all before.

ctx.s: 虽然是{老生常谈}，但我还是要提醒大家：出门注意安全。
ctx.en: It may be the same old advice, but I still have to remind everyone: stay safe when you go out.

ctx.s: “多读书、多练习”听起来像{老生常谈}，其实是学语言最有效的办法。
ctx.en: "Read more, practise more" sounds like a platitude, but it's actually the most effective way to learn a language.

ctx.s: 每次开会，经理强调的都是“注意安全、按时交货”这些{老生常谈}，可大家都知道这很重要。
ctx.en: At every meeting the manager stresses the same familiar points, "safety first, deliver on time", yet everyone knows they matter.

ctx.s: 你说的这些{老生常谈}，我耳朵都快听出茧子了。
ctx.en: I've heard these same old lines of yours so often my ears are practically calloused.

ctx.s: 他的发言都是{老生常谈}吗？不，最后那个建议还挺新鲜的。
ctx.en: Was his speech all platitudes? No, that last suggestion was actually quite fresh.

bad.s: 我们俩是{老生常谈}的朋友，认识二十年了。
bad.en: (meant: we are old friends who often chat; we've known each other twenty years)
bad.why: It means familiar, often-repeated words, not a long friendship or chatting often.

bad.s: 这位老教授讲课很新颖，真是{老生常谈}。
bad.en: (meant: the old professor teaches in a fresh way)
bad.why: It says the words are stale and familiar; it cannot praise an old person's fresh ideas.

mean: ingenious, coming up with something original
lit: to bring out a design of one's own mind, different from everyone else's

use.how: Predicate, or adverbial with 地: 他别出心裁地…. Praises a design, plan or idea that is original and clever.

near.diff: 标新立异 is being different on purpose, often a criticism of showing off; 别出心裁 praises a genuinely clever original idea.

cue: Instead of a normal menu, a café prints its dishes on old record sleeves, and every customer remarks on how clever and unusual the idea is. How is it?

ctx.s: 这家咖啡馆的装修{别出心裁}，墙上挂满了旧唱片。
ctx.en: This café's decor is wonderfully original; the walls are covered with old records.

ctx.s: 他{别出心裁}地用折纸做了一张生日贺卡。
ctx.en: He had the clever idea of making a birthday card out of origami.

ctx.s: “谁想出来的这个包装？真是{别出心裁}！”
ctx.en: "Who came up with this packaging? What an original idea!"

ctx.s: 老师{别出心裁}，让学生用演话剧的方式复习课文。
ctx.en: The teacher had an inventive idea: the students reviewed the lesson by acting it out as a play.

ctx.s: 今年的晚会开场{别出心裁}，观众都很惊喜。
ctx.en: This year's gala opened in a highly original way, and the audience was delighted.

ctx.s: 这次设计比赛，评委最看重的就是作品是否{别出心裁}。
ctx.en: In this design contest, what the judges value most is whether an entry is original.

bad.s: 他{别出心裁}地抄了别人的作业。
bad.en: (meant: he cleverly copied someone else's homework)
bad.why: It praises original creativity; copying is the opposite, and it is never used for cheating.

bad.s: 这个人很{别出心裁}，总想骗别人的钱。
bad.en: (meant: this person is crafty and always trying to cheat people)
bad.why: It praises inventive ideas, not scheming; it can never describe someone out to cheat others.

lit: to have some other purpose in one's mind

use.how: Predicate or attributive (别有用心的人). Accuses someone of hiding a selfish or harmful purpose behind what they say or do.

near.diff: 居心叵测 is darker and more formal: intentions too sinister to fathom; 别有用心 is simply a hidden motive behind an act.

cue: A stranger keeps offering to help you invest your savings and asks for your bank details. You suspect a hidden purpose. How would you describe him?

ctx.s: 他突然对我这么热情，我总觉得他{别有用心}。
ctx.en: He's suddenly so warm towards me; I can't help feeling he's up to something.

ctx.s: 有些{别有用心}的商家，故意夸大产品的效果。
ctx.en: Some unscrupulous sellers deliberately exaggerate what their products can do.

ctx.s: “你别把我想得那么坏，我帮你真的不是{别有用心}。”
ctx.en: "Don't think so badly of me; I'm really not helping you for some ulterior motive."

ctx.s: 这条谣言显然是有人{别有用心}地编造出来的。
ctx.en: This rumour was clearly made up by someone with an agenda.

ctx.s: 她问了我好多公司的事，是好奇，还是{别有用心}？
ctx.en: She asked me so much about the company; was she just curious, or did she have a motive?

ctx.s: 网上那些“免费领奖”的链接，往往是{别有用心}的人设下的陷阱。
ctx.en: Those "claim your free prize" links online are often traps set by people with bad intentions.

bad.s: 妈妈{别有用心}地给我做了一桌好菜，庆祝我考上大学。
bad.en: (meant: mum lovingly cooked a feast to celebrate my getting into university)
bad.why: It implies a hidden selfish motive, which insults a mother's loving effort; it is never used for sincere care.

bad.s: 这个设计{别有用心}，非常有创意。
bad.en: (meant: this design is original and creative)
bad.why: It accuses someone of a hidden motive; it cannot praise a design for being original.

mean: having put much careful thought into it for another's sake
lit: the intention is deep and the care painstaking

use.how: Predicate, often in 真是用心良苦 or 可谓用心良苦, or as a noun (…的用心良苦). Said of someone whose careful, often unnoticed effort was for another's good.

near.diff: 煞费苦心 only says someone went to great pains, for any end, even a bad one; 用心良苦 implies the care was well meant for others.

cue: Your coach was harsh on you all season, and only after you won the final did you realise he had done it all to make you stronger. How were his efforts?

ctx.s: 爸爸不让你玩手机，是怕你耽误学习，真是{用心良苦}。
ctx.en: Dad won't let you play on your phone because he's afraid it'll hurt your studies; he really means well.

ctx.s: 长大以后，我才明白妈妈当年的{用心良苦}。
ctx.en: Only after growing up did I understand how much thought my mother put into everything back then.

ctx.s: 老师故意给他打低分，原来是想激励他，可谓{用心良苦}。
ctx.en: The teacher gave him a low mark on purpose to spur him on; it was all for his sake.

ctx.s: “你知道教练为什么天天骂你吗？他是{用心良苦}啊！”
ctx.en: "Do you know why the coach yells at you every day? It's all for your own good!"

ctx.s: 这本教材故意不给答案，编者{用心良苦}，是想让学生自己思考。
ctx.en: This textbook deliberately gives no answers; the editors mean well: they want the students to think for themselves.

ctx.s: 这部电影的结局让人心酸，导演{用心良苦}，就是想让观众珍惜身边的人。
ctx.en: The film's ending is heartbreaking, but the director meant it for the audience's good: to make them cherish the people around them.

bad.s: 小偷{用心良苦}地研究了这家银行的监控。
bad.en: (meant: the thief carefully studied the bank's cameras)
bad.why: It implies good intentions towards someone else, so it cannot describe a criminal's careful scheming.

bad.s: 我这次考试{用心良苦}，终于考了满分。
bad.en: (meant: I worked hard for this exam and finally got full marks)
bad.why: It is about care taken for another person's sake, not about one's own hard work for one's own goal.

use.how: A noun, usually after 是 or 也是: 紧张是人之常情。 Said to explain or excuse a feeling or reaction anyone would have.

near.diff: 理所当然 is anything that obviously should be so; 人之常情 is specifically a natural human feeling or reaction.

cue: A friend is embarrassed that she cried at her farewell party after ten years at the company. You tell her anyone would feel the same. What is crying, you say?

ctx.s: 第一次上台紧张，这是{人之常情}。
ctx.en: Being nervous the first time you go on stage is only human.

ctx.s: 想家是{人之常情}，你不用不好意思。
ctx.en: Being homesick is perfectly natural; no need to be embarrassed.

ctx.s: “他失业了心情不好，也是{人之常情}，你多体谅他吧。”
ctx.en: "He's lost his job, so of course he's in a bad mood; try to be understanding."

ctx.s: 孩子考砸了，父母一时生气也是{人之常情}，过后好好谈谈就行。
ctx.en: When a child fails an exam, it's only human for the parents to get angry for a moment; just talk it over calmly afterwards.

ctx.s: 喜欢听好话是{人之常情}，但也要听得进批评。
ctx.en: Everyone likes to hear compliments, but you also have to be able to take criticism.

ctx.s: 难道希望家人平安不是{人之常情}吗？
ctx.en: Isn't wanting your family to be safe the most natural thing in the world?

bad.s: 太阳从东边升起是{人之常情}。
bad.en: (meant: it's natural and obvious that the sun rises in the east)
bad.why: It is about human feelings and reactions, not facts of nature like the sunrise.

bad.s: 他是个很{人之常情}的人，大家都喜欢他。
bad.en: (meant: he is a very warm, human person)
bad.why: It names a natural reaction, not a trait; it cannot describe a person's character or be modified by 'very'.

lit: the whole world fixes its eyes on it

use.how: Mostly attributive (举世瞩目的成就) or predicate. Used in news and formal writing of events and achievements the whole world watches.

near.diff: 举世闻名 is being famous all over the world; 举世瞩目 is drawing the world's attention, usually to an event or achievement now.

cue: Billions of people on every continent are glued to their screens for the first crewed landing on Mars. What kind of event is it?

ctx.s: 奥运会开幕式是一场{举世瞩目}的盛会。
ctx.en: The Olympic opening ceremony is a grand event the whole world watches.

ctx.s: 这项登月计划取得了{举世瞩目}的成功。
ctx.en: The moon-landing programme achieved a success that drew attention around the world.

ctx.s: 世界杯决赛今晚举行，这场{举世瞩目}的比赛将吸引数十亿观众。
ctx.en: The World Cup final is tonight; this match, followed worldwide, will draw billions of viewers.

ctx.s: 这项考古发现一经公布，便成为{举世瞩目}的焦点。
ctx.en: As soon as the archaeological find was announced, it became the focus of worldwide attention.

ctx.s: 她在国际比赛中连夺三枚金牌，成绩{举世瞩目}。
ctx.en: She won three gold medals in a row at the international championships, a result that caught the world's eye.

ctx.s: 这座跨海大桥的建成，被媒体称为{举世瞩目}的工程奇迹。
ctx.en: The media called the completion of the sea-crossing bridge an engineering marvel that captured world attention.

bad.s: 我的新发型在班里{举世瞩目}。
bad.en: (meant: my new haircut got everyone's attention in class)
bad.why: Its first half means the whole world; it cannot be limited to one class, and it is far too grand for a haircut.

bad.s: 全世界都{举世瞩目}这场比赛。
bad.en: (meant: the whole world is watching this match)
bad.why: It already means 'the whole world watches' and takes no object; the match itself should be the subject.

mean: to fly into a thunderous rage at someone
lit: to let loose a great clap of thunder

use.how: Predicate, often 对某人大发雷霆. Describes a sudden, loud outburst of anger, typically by someone with authority over the listener.

near.diff: 暴跳如雷 pictures someone stamping and roaring out of control; 大发雷霆 is a big loud outburst, often a boss or parent scolding.

cue: The manager discovers the report sent to the client was full of errors and starts shouting so loudly that the whole office goes silent. What did the manager do?

ctx.s: 爸爸看到我的成绩单，{大发雷霆}。
ctx.en: When Dad saw my report card, he exploded with rage.

ctx.s: 老板因为一个小错误对他{大发雷霆}，他委屈极了。
ctx.en: The boss blew up at him over a tiny mistake, and he felt terribly wronged.

ctx.s: “别为这点小事{大发雷霆}，先冷静一下。”
ctx.en: "Don't fly into a rage over such a small thing; calm down first."

ctx.s: 项目又推迟了，总经理在会上{大发雷霆}，把大家骂了一顿。
ctx.en: The project was delayed again, and the general manager stormed at everyone in the meeting.

ctx.s: 平时温和的王老师，那天竟然{大发雷霆}，全班都吓坏了。
ctx.en: Mr Wang, usually so gentle, actually erupted in anger that day, and the whole class was terrified.

ctx.s: 你明知道他脾气不好，为什么还要做让他{大发雷霆}的事？
ctx.en: You know he has a temper, so why do things that make him blow up?

bad.s: 今晚{大发雷霆}，我们别出门了。
bad.en: (meant: there's a big thunderstorm tonight, let's stay in)
bad.why: It describes a person's rage only, never real thunder or weather.

bad.s: 听到好消息，他高兴得{大发雷霆}。
bad.en: (meant: hearing the good news, he shouted for joy)
bad.why: It means an outburst of anger; it cannot express joy or excitement.
